notes.s: Jungkook's solo: a happiness so complete he suspects it of being a dream.
notes.t: Jungkook's solo, released April 2018 as the theme for Love Yourself 起 Wonder, with no album to live on until 結 Answer collected it months later. Chronologically it opens the four-solo arc that fans read as one story: wonder here, then Serendipity, Singularity and Epiphany. The video revisits locations from the 화양연화 videos, which is why the storyline-tracking side of the fandom treats it as a reward track. It wins ARMY's best-B-side polls with some regularity.
k: 재림 is the Second Coming, specifically the Christian one, and carries no casual sense in Korean. Childhood dreams returning get described with the vocabulary of prophesied divine return, which is the first instance of a habit the whole Love Yourself series has, borrowing salvation words for a love song. Serendipity's 구원 and Save ME's 구해줘 are the same move.
내 안 깊은 곳의 A priori

Left in Latin in the Korean lyric. A priori knowledge is what you hold before any experience of the world, so the claim is that she was in him before they ever met. That is the series' argument about fate stated as epistemology, and Serendipity restates it in plainer words.

신기루 is a mirage. Four lines in, the song concedes that the dream may be an optical trick in a desert, and everything sung afterwards is sung with that concession standing. It turns the later plea not to wake up into something closer to fear than to bliss.

Two concessive endings back to back, both meaning even if. -ㄴ대도 contracts -ㄴ다고 해도, so it is even if they say it does, one step further removed than a plain -아도. Stacking concessives is the standard Korean way to build a no-matter-what chorus, and spotting the pattern makes a lot of other bridges readable.
